newsitem.title: USA: Alumax looking forward to second half.
newsitem.headline: Alumax looking forward to second half.

text.p: Alumax Inc is looking forward to the second half of 1997, Chief Executive Officer Allen Born said Tuesday.

"Firm orders and good aluminum volumes reflect positive world economic growth. Visible inventories are trending downward, and market conditions will ultimately reflect the impact of continued inventory drawdowns."

The company reported second-quarter 1997 earnings of $35.8 million, or $0.64 per share, compared with $83.1 million, or $1.77 a share a year ago when there was a gain of $55.1 million, or $1.21 a share, on the sale of mining investments.

Earnings from operations in the second quarter were $71.0 million on sales of $730.9 million and aluminum shipments of 260,600 metric tonnes. This compares with earnings from operations of $64.4 million on sales of $851.4 million and shipments of 283,300 tonnes in the second quarter of 1996.
"Alumax earnings excluding nonrecurring items continued to trend upward during the second quarter," Born said.
"Stronger operating results are benefitting from better average pricing for our products," he noted.

"While our overall revenues and shipments were lower than in 1996, reflecting the strategic sale of several of our fabricated products businesses in September 1996, they were above first-quarter 1997 levels, evidencing firm demand for our products." ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
